security_audit.summary: Most static command and blocker findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline file references, comments, CSS, and JavaScript RegExp.exec. The confirmed issues are low-severity third-party network dependencies for cdnjs p5.js and Google Fonts. No evidence found of prompt injection, shell execution, credential access, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js locally or add subresource integrity and version pinning for the CDN script.
Use local fonts, system fonts, or clearly disclose that generated artifacts contact Google font domains.
Document which remote assets are loaded and provide an offline template option for restricted environments.

content.value_statement: Generative art prompts often lack structure, repeatability, and interactive controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create p5.js art with seeded variation.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of an algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Provides a p5.js HTML viewer template with sidebar controls.
Uses seeded randomness through randomSeed and noiseSeed patterns.
Defines seed navigation, parameter sliders, color controls, and reset behavior.
Includes JavaScript reference patterns for parameters, classes, utilities, and image export.
limitations: Generated artifacts depend on p5.js from a CDN unless assets are bundled locally.
The viewer template contains placeholder algorithm sections that must be completed.
It does not provide backend storage, collaboration, or gallery publishing.
Visual quality depends on the prompt and the model implementation.

use_cases.title: Prototype Interactive Art
use_cases.description: Create a browser-ready p5.js sketch with controls for seed, parameters, and colors.

use_cases.title: Teach Generative Systems
use_cases.description: Demonstrate seeded randomness, particle systems, flow fields, and parameter tuning in one artifact.

use_cases.title: Explore Visual Concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a concept into an algorithmic philosophy and a reproducible generative artwork.

prompt_templates.title: Start Simple
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one generative artwork.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece about quiet ocean currents. Include the philosophy and a single interactive p5.js HTML artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Parameters
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants interactive control over a clear visual system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create seeded generative art based on botanical growth. Add sliders for density, branching, curve tension, and growth speed.

prompt_templates.title: Build Variations
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a reproducible family of outputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a generative art system for urban light patterns. Include seed navigation and identify three strong seed variations.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced System Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced user requests a richer algorithmic structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a philosophy-driven p5.js artwork using interacting fields, particle trails, palette controls, and performance-aware animation.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by wind moving through tall grass.
output_examples.output: A short algorithmic philosophy, followed by an interactive p5.js artifact with seed controls, motion parameters, and color tuning.

output_examples.input: Make 100 reproducible visual variations of a crystalline growth system.
output_examples.output: A single browser artifact with seed navigation, repeatable randomness, and controls for cell density, symmetry, and palette.

output_examples.input: Build a particle-based artwork for a calm installation screen.
output_examples.output: A p5.js viewer using slow particle motion, adjustable trail length, reproducible seeds, and a reset control.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual concept before choosing particle, field, or geometry methods.
Keep seeded randomness enabled so every important output can be reproduced.
Expose only meaningful parameters that change the artwork without breaking composition.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a known artist style or ask for direct imitation.
Do not replace the template structure before confirming required controls still work.
Do not add random parameters that make the artwork noisy or hard to tune.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates philosophy-driven p5.js generative art with interactive controls and reproducible seeds.

faq.question: Can the output run in a browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The intended output is a single HTML artifact that can run in a browser.

faq.question: Does it require a server?
faq.answer: No. The viewer is designed as a standalone HTML file, although it may load p5.js from a CDN.

faq.question: Can I change colors and parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. The template supports sliders, color controls, seed navigation, and reset behavior.

faq.question: Does the same seed create the same art?
faq.answer: Yes, when the generated algorithm uses the provided seeded randomness patterns correctly.

faq.question: Is this for copying existing artist styles?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for original algorithmic concepts rather than direct imitation.
